metadata.scenario_context: A group of software developers from different multinational companies plan to meet during the first week of May for an annual conference. One of developers are contemplating joining a strike in protest of the low wages in their sector.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Denmark strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Kazakhstan strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the feasibility of organizing the conference on May 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, have you thought about the timing of the conference? May 1st seems like it could be a challenging date. 

Also... is it common in our field to discuss or even join strikes for issues like wages? I'm curious about that perspective.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Peter, yeah, I’ve been thinking about the dates. The first week of May could work, but I agree, May 1st might be tricky with the holiday. 

As for strikes, well... from where I come from, we don’t really join strikes. It's just not something we do. I think there are better ways to address wage issues. What do you think about the other dates?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Peter
shared_prefix.message:
I totally agree with you about May 1st being tricky. We should probably consider other dates that won’t conflict with holidays. 

But about the strikes... I still find it surprising that people see it as an option. I just don’t understand how that can be a productive approach. What do you think motivates developers to consider joining a strike?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I mean, I don't really see meaningful differences here. Developers everywhere have their own ways of tackling issues. At the end of the day, it's all the same—everyone wants to get their point across. People figure it out one way or another. 

But back to the conference dates, maybe we should look at the 3rd or 5th? Those seem more straightforward without any holiday conflicts. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
